Subject: Discovery recap & integration/onboarding plan — FastRetail PoC

Thanks for taking the time today, Alex — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes during peak checkout flows causing cart abandonment (~300-400ms SLA currently missed)
- High per-token cost on current 3rd-party API with unpredictable throttling
- Strict PCI-adjacent requirements: no customer PII persisted in vendor logs; audit logging required

Current stack and constraints:
- Backend: Node.js services (AWS Fargate), primary language for ML integration: TypeScript/Node
- Existing model calls go through a third-party API via server-side calls from checkout service
- Peak QPS: ~120 requests/sec during promotions; typical payload size ~150-300 tokens

Success criteria for PoC:
1) Average p50 latency below 90ms for single-turn generation workloads during non-peak; p95 < 220ms under expected PoC load
2) Token cost reduction of >=30% vs current provider with similar output quality
3) Demonstrable audit logs (request ids, redacted inputs) retained for 90 days in customer-managed store or via our Private option

Proposed PoC scope & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff and access — we’ll provision a temporary dedicated instance and share credentials (scoped)
- Week 1: Integration (SDK + sample endpoints) — Node/TypeScript SDK, sample wrapper to mirror your checkout call patterns
- Week 2: Load testing & tuning — run synthetic peak tests; adjust batching and quantization profile
- Week 3: Validation & quality checks — run your customer-facing prompts through both systems for parity checks

Owners (Redwood / FastRetail):
- Redwood: Ben Carter (sales/PoC owner) — provisioning + infra coordination
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (solutions engineer) — integration support, SDK snippets, load tuning
- FastRetail: Alex Kim — product lead; Priya Singh — engineering lead for integration

SDK & API compatibility notes:
- We’ll provide our Node.js/TypeScript SDK (npm package) and a simple Express middleware snippet to drop into your checkout service.
- If you need Python examples for backend jobs, we can include a minimal Python client as well.
- API supports streaming + non-streaming responses; for checkout we recommend non-streaming single-shot calls to keep determinism and latency predictable.

Attachments:
- I’ve attached an initial integration_plan_v1.pdf with milestones and a simple sequence diagram for the checkout flow.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the two engineering contacts (Alex and Priya) are the right people?
2) I'll send a calendar invite for a kick-off meeting (30 min) — suggested times: Thu 10:00am or Fri 11:00am PT.
3) We’ll need a test API key and a staging endpoint (w/ representative payload) to start integration by Monday.

Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Best,
Ben
